chunk_findings.detail: `urllib.request.build_opener(_HTTPHandler, _HTTPSHandler)` passes the handler classes, not instances. `OpenerDirector.add_handler` expects an instance and invokes `handler.add_parent(self)`; when `handler` is a class this raises `TypeError` (`add_parent() missing 1 required positional argument: 'parent'`). Concrete input: `UrllibHttpClient().request("GET", "http://example.com", timeout=1, on_connect=lambda c: None)` crashes before any request is sent, so the socket-abort path is completely broken and the error is not an `HttpError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/http.py:_tracked_opener

chunk_findings.detail: `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)` runs outside the `try` block and raises `ValueError` for malformed network URLs, e.g. `"http://[[REDACTED:ipv6]"` raises `ValueError: Invalid IPv6 URL`. That escapes the adapter as `ValueError`, not an `HttpError`/`OSError`, violating the documented “Raises only `HttpError` subclasses” contract and defeating callers that migrate by catching `OSError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/http.py:require_http_url

chunk_findings.detail: The `except urllib.error.HTTPError` handler catches every `HTTPError`, but urllib turns each non-2xx response into an `HTTPError` unless a redirect handler follows it. A server returning `304 Not Modified` is not followed, so with the default `raise_for_status=True` the adapter raises `HttpStatusError(status=304)` despite the module/class documentation and the unused `STATUS_ERROR_FLOOR = 400` saying `HttpStatusError` is only raised for status >= 400. This makes normal conditional GETs fail.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/http.py:UrllibHttpClient.request

chunk_findings.detail: A server that sends a non-HTTP status line causes `http.client` to raise `http.client.BadStatusLine` (an `http.client.HTTPException`), but urllib wraps exceptions from `getresponse` in `urllib.error.URLError`. `_classify` checks `URLError` first and returns `HttpConnectionError`, even though the module explicitly classifies “an answer that is not valid HTTP” as `HttpProtocolError`. Example: an HTTP endpoint responding `b'not-http\r\n'` is mislabeled as `kind="connection"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/http.py:_classify

chunk_findings.detail: `_get` selects the client with `(client or default_client())`. The `HttpClient` protocol imposes no truthiness contract, so a valid client implementation whose `__bool__` returns `False` (for example a recording fake that reports false when it has no responses) is silently ignored and `default_client()` is used instead. That makes the optional injection point unreliable and can cause a real network request in code or tests that explicitly supplied a fake; it should be `client if client is not None else default_client()`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/release_index.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: A slow remote URL that accepts the TCP connection but never responds will make `HttpClient.request` raise `TimeoutError` (the chat path in this same file still catches `TimeoutError` explicitly). `TimeoutError` is an `OSError` subclass, not an `HttpError`, so this handler does not run and the timeout propagates to the caller instead of returning `False` as the old `except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError)` did. That changes behavior and can crash a review discovery when a checked URL times out.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/engine.py:600 (`except HttpError` in `_remote_url_ok`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new test imports `http.client` directly to build `BadStatusLine`, but the HTTP adapter contract in this change says only the home module (`ddflow/adapters/http.py`) may import `urllib.request`, `http.client`, or `socket`. This non-home import adds a new architecture violator and can trip the `importlinter-http-home` guard or force the baseline to grow, which violates the “baseline ignore lists only shrink” constraint in [D-adapters-answers]. The test can pass an already-exported adapter exception or a locally constructed cause instead.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_key_file.py:314

chunk_findings.detail: The contract for this change is that only the home module `ddflow/adapters/` imports `urllib.request`, `http.client`, or `socket`. The test `test_other_http_client_errors_are_named_and_never_retried_as_truncation` still has a direct `import http.client` inside it, so this file outside the home imports a low-level HTTP library. The new `tests/guard_baselines/importlinter-http-home.toml` guard enforces exactly one allowed importer, so this import violates the contract and will make the architecture guard fail (or otherwise contradict the change’s own stated boundary).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_defaults.py:265

chunk_findings.detail: `_real_adapters` instantiates `ScriptedUrllib(monkeypatch)` which uses the test framework's `monkeypatch` fixture directly from a helper function rather than receiving it or handling it cleanly through a test parameter, causing tests that invoke `_real_adapters()` without arguments (such as `test_every_fake_has_a_conformance_case_and_a_real_adapter` when called without parameters or through helper code) to fail if `monkeypatch` is omitted or uninitialized.
